messages:
mia (docs): Draft PR #8024 updates the rate limits and quota guide: swaps old header to x-rw-usage-plan, adds a Go SDK snippet, and fixes the dashboard anchor. Can someone quick-check wording and the PromQL before I land? https://confluence.redwood/internal/docs/quota-and-pricing
ash (eng): Quick check: which dashboard anchor did you point to? We renamed panels last week.
mia (docs): Pointing to dashboard?id=plan-usage-main and I added the metric name in parentheses. Also included a short migration note: 'Legacy header x-rw-quota is supported and maps to x-rw-usage-plan.'
tori (product): UX prefers 'grace credits' in user-facing docs (internal docs can keep 'burst' in parentheses). Also please add a one-sentence behavior note: 'Grace credits are deducted before plan quota and do not refill mid-cycle.'
baen (analytics): Small analytics nit: call the metric tokens_consumed_total in the doc and add this PromQL so folks can reproduce the panel:
```
sum(rate(tokens_consumed_total{plan=~"(free|pro|enterprise)"}[5m])) by (plan)
```
mia (docs): Thanks — will paste that. I added a Go example for the SDK since we don't have many Go snippets for usage yet. Draft Go snippet:
```
import "github.com/redwoodinc/redwood"
client := redwood.NewClient("${TOKEN}")
client.Headers.Set("x-rw-usage-plan", "enterprise")
resp, _ := client.Get("/v1/usage")
fmt.Println(string(resp.Body))
```
ash (eng): Go snippet looks fine. Tiny nit: prefer NewClientWithTimeout(30*time.Second) in examples to avoid hanging in dev tests.
mia (docs): Good call, I'll update the snippet. @ci-bot can we run docs lint on the branch once I push?
ci-bot: docs-ci: lint & build started for PR #8024
ben (analytics): One more suggestion: add a short note about billing slabs wording — use 'tiered slabs' and link to the pricing CSV. Keep the in-doc text short and link to the canonical CSV URL.
ci-bot: docs-ci: lint & build passed \u2705
mia (docs): Merged PR #8024 after updating the Go snippet with timeout and adding the PromQL and slab note. Backfilled redirect for old header anchor. Closing thread — thanks!
